messages:
lee: Heads-up — ap-southeast1 tiny-gpu queue creeping, many pods Pending with 'FailedScheduling' but node capacity exists. Observed many short-lived attach/detach events from the warmpool nodes. Anyone seeing attach churn?

olivia: confirming. I see attach/detach flaps in gce-controller logs around 03:12. nvme attach times spike and then kubelet marks NodeReady false for ~30s.

nina: netops also flagged a regional interconnect retransmit increase at ~03:10. traceroutes show an asymmetry b/w 1a and 1c.

lee: that matches the attach timeouts — block device ops timing out when control-plane egress retries increased. Pods bound to nodes then get evicted, scheduler immediately rebinding -> tiny slot fragmentation because pods land across AZs.

kai: mitigation idea: 1) add a temporary `warmpool/frag-mitigation=true:PreferNoSchedule` node-label so scheduler avoids bouncing tiny-gpu across AZs 2) lower scheduler bind concurrency for the tiny-gpu queue 3) bump warmpool target up by 2 to absorb drains.

olivia: +1. Also can we change the attach/detach controller's retry window? Short-term we can set a higher attach timeout to reduce false detach.

lee: commands I'd run now: 
```
# add prefernoschedule label to nodes in the warmpool (can be removed later)
kubectl label nodes node-xyz warmpool-frag=avoid --overwrite
# tweak scheduler via k8s-configmap rollout (canary):
kubectl -n kube-system set env deployment/kube-scheduler SCHED_BIND_CONCURRENCY=6 --record
# scale warmpool
kubectl scale deployment/warmpool-ap-southeast1 --replicas=14 -n infra
```

infra-bot: [autoscaler] warmpool-ap-southeast1 requested scale 12 -> 14 by @lee. Scaling initiated.

ops-bot: [gce] detected attach/detach error burst on nodes [node-xyz,node-abc] at 2026-03-18T03:11:58Z. Forwarded to cloud provider ticket CLOUD-10012.

nina: good catch. I'll keep traceroutes and attach traces in the ticket. We should also tune alerting: warmpool attach failures currently alert at 10% error rate for 10m — consider lowering to 2m for quicker response.

kai: longer-term action: scheduler should implement a per-pod exponential backoff on bind attempts when a node from the same AZ recently failed -> avoid oscillation across AZ boundary. Filing INF-4080.

olivia: filed INF-4080: "scheduler: per-pod bind backoff and AZ-aware rebinds to reduce warm-pool fragmentation". Assigned to eng-platform.

lee: update 03:21 — scale completed, preemption rate dropped ~45%, pending tiny-gpu decreased. Attach failures still show small spikes but system is stable.

nina: will follow up with NetOps postmortem and cloud provider logs. Also propose a short runbook: if warmpool attach/detach spikes -> scale + set preferNoSchedule label + reduce scheduler bind concurrency, wait 10m.

kai: agreed. I'll draft the runbook and PR for the scheduler change. Thanks team.

lee: closing for now, leaving labels in place for 30m then revert. If cloud confirms underlying interconnect issue we'll keep mitigations and schedule RFC. :thumbsup:
